items.title: What do employers usually look for in hiring?

values: Materials and setup｜fully fictional

You are only a career explorer compiling a set of fictional public exercise records, and do not play a police officer or dispatcher. A1: a fictional call record says that on Tuesday at 18:20 a lost bicycle was seen at the north gate, and the caller provided no vehicle description.
A2: a fictional gatekeeper's log says that on Tuesday at 18:05 a bicycle was found at the south gate, and the person logging it wrote only “blue,” with no plate or number recorded.
A3: a fictional owner's message says the owner only noticed on Wednesday morning that the bicycle was gone and cannot remember where it was last parked.
Tasks and outputs
Make a three-column table: material number｜verifiable original fact｜unknown or conflicting. Write out the time, place, and information source for A1, A2, and A3 one by one.

Then write a handover card: make the differences between the north and south gates and between Tuesday and Wednesday explicit, and list the questions authorized personnel need to verify; do not judge whether it is the same bicycle and do not propose on-scene action.
Reference answers (do it independently first)

A1: the call record states Tuesday 18:20, north gate, a lost bicycle seen; the vehicle description and the basis for identification are unknown. A2: the gatekeeper's log states Tuesday 18:05, south gate, a blue bicycle; the vehicle number and whether it is the same bicycle as in A1 are unknown. A3: the owner's message states the bicycle was noticed missing on Wednesday morning; 
the last parking time, the place, and the actual time of loss are all unknown.

Reference handover card: for authorized personnel to verify ① on what basis the A1 caller determined the bicycle was lost, and whether a description can be given; ② whether the A2 bicycle has a verifiable number, and whether the log time and place are accurate; ③ the last confirmed time, place, and features of the A3 bicycle; ④ whether the three materials concern the same bicycle. Report only the source statements and the unknowns; do not merge the north or south gate and Tuesday 
or Wednesday into a confirmed incident, and do not propose on-scene action.
Boundaries and scoring

Five points, one each: the three sources kept separate, times accurate, the place conflict clearly marked, unknowns not filled in, and handover only without acting on your own.；The exercise involves no real emergency calls, stops, tracking, on-scene searches, or evidence handling; real incidents must go through official local channels.

Case investigation｜the investigation role collects, verifies, and organizes evidence within its authority｜procedural requirements follow the jurisdiction. — 25/100; weight=1/3; police-and-detectives.profile.responsibilities-block.1[3]

Record and report｜state known facts, open questions, the basis for action, and the responsible person｜contradictions must not be omitted. — 75/100; weight=1/3; police-and-detectives.profile.responsibilities-block.1[4]

title.text: Police and detectives: work tasks, wage definitions, and the entry path

subject.name: Police and Detectives
subject.summary: Police officers and detectives protect people and property, respond to incidents, patrol, collect and verify leads, and create records and hand over cases under lawful authorization and agency procedures. This page uses the US BLS Police and Detectives Occupational Outlook Handbook combined definition as the statistical reference; that combination also includes fish and game enforcement and transit and railroad police. The tasks and wages of patrol 33-3051 and investigation 33-3021 are verified separately, and US conditions cannot be treated as Chinese recruitment standards.
